extracted.intended_audience: people interested in science communication and editing (science editors, publishers, authors, and related professionals)
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of an editors' professional association (EASE) and the standards/guidelines it promotes for science journals, authors, and publishers — including reporting sex/gender, support for non-native-English authors, multilingual republication, and environmental/sustainability practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of international standards for science journals
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerns of the organization included the development of international standards for science journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EASE's mission is 'to improve the global standard and quality of science editing' by promoting the value of science editors and supporting professional development, research, and collaboration. This implies promoting common, international editorial standards and best practices for journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for authors whose first language was not English
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines for authors whose first language was not English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EASE has worked on guidance to help non-native English-speaking authors prepare manuscripts suitable for publication, as part of its efforts to raise manuscript quality and accessibility across language barriers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Republishing of articles in multiple languages
rubrics_metrics.description: Republishing of articles in multiple languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EASE has expressed concern and provided input on policies/practices around multilingual republication to increase accessibility and dissemination of research across language communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvement of science communication generally
rubrics_metrics.description: The improvement of science communication generally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad editorial and communicative quality criteria for how scientific findings are reported and presented to different audiences; EASE promotes professional development and collaboration to achieve this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sex and Gender Equity in Research (SAGER) Guidelines / gender- and sex-sensitive reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Sex and Gender Equity in Research (SAGER) Guidelines — the first reporting guidelines to encourage systematic reporting of sex and gender dimensions in scholarly publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Developed and published by the EASE Gender Policy Committee to advance gender- and sex-sensitive reporting and communication in science. The SAGER guidelines are listed in EQUATOR, have been translated into multiple languages (Chinese, Korean, Portuguese, Spanish, Turkish, Vietnamese), and have been adopted by a number of journals. They serve as explicit criteria for authors and editors to report sex/gender dimensions systematically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing gender bias in reporting (EASE Gender Policy Committee)
rubrics_metrics.description: EASE established a Gender Policy Committee to address the gender bias in the reporting of scholarly articles in scientific journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee's remit is to advance gender- and sex-sensitive reporting and communication; its work includes consultative development of reporting guidelines (SAGER) and advocacy for editorial policies that reduce gender bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental sustainability and SDG-aligned publishing practices (Environmental Manifesto)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication of a 2021 Environmental Manifesto outlining a variety of environmentally responsible actions for publishers and others to support the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manifesto recommends actions such as digital publication, improving journal distribution, the role of editors in sustainability, adoption of an environment policy, and broader improvements in office, employee, food, and building management. These are criteria/policies publishers and editors can adopt to make publishing more environmentally responsible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement with formal standards bodies (ISO/BSI liaison and representation)
rubrics_metrics.description: EASE has category A liaison status with the International Organization for Standardization (Technical Committee 46/subcommittee 9) and is represented on committees of the British Standards Institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This affiliation signals participation in the creation and adoption of formal standards relevant to documentation, information management, and publishing; editors/journals are encouraged to align practices with relevant ISO/BSI standards where appropriate.
